title: Call graph compact signature proposal
content:
Context / problem statement:

This is a personal scratchpad for a compact, forward-compatible "call graph" signature format we could use between clients (SDKs/proxies/edge) and Redwood inference routers/serving-runtime.  The goal is to encode intent + minimal provenance for multi-hop calls (tool calls, function calling, nested LLM tool chains) in a size-efficient, easily-parsable envelope that:

- stays tiny for mobile/edge telemetry budgets
- supports version negotiation and graceful fallback when servers or clients don't understand new fields
- is expressive enough to support tracing, security assertions, and lightweight routing hints (latency/cost)

This doc is intentionally rough: design ideas, ASCII diagrams, wire-shape sketches, and open questions.

Outcomes we want:
- a canonical compact header that SDKs and proxies can emit for each request
- server-side libraries that can parse/validate and extract routing/telemetry/ACL hints
- a compatibility story so new fields don't break older components

Principles / constraints:
- Keep header < 512 bytes most of the time (target 128-256 bytes typical)
- Binary-first (CBOR-like) but canonical text fallback (base64 or short JSON) for debugging
- Versioned with small integer v-tags and a short feature bitset for optional features
- No heavy crypto requirement by default; optional attachments for signatures/HSM assertions

High-level shape (informal):
- magic + version (1 byte magic, 1 byte version)
- compact feature bitset (variable-length varint)
- caller identity (short id, 4-8 bytes) or anonymous flag
- call-tree fingerprint (rolling-hash of function/tool names up to N hops, truncated e.g. 64b)
- input tokenization signature (short hash) optional
- routing hint byte (enum: prefer-latency / prefer-cost / require-region / pinned-model)
- optional metadata TLV sequence (k/v pairs with small keys)

ASCII diagram (logical fields):

[MAGIC|V] [FEATbits] [CALLER_ID] [TREE_FP] [TOK_FP?] [ROUTE] [TLV*]

where TLV is repeated small items: k(len<=8), v(len<=64).  Keys are drawn from a global short key registry (e.g. k=0x01 => request-id, 0x02 => parent-call-id).

Wire examples (pseudo-CBOR as readable hex-ish):
- v1 minimal anonymous: 0x7A 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00 (MAGIC,ver,feats=0,caller=0,tree_fp=0)
- v1 full: [0x7A,0x01,0x05, caller=0x12A3, tree_fp=0x9f4b..., route=0x02, TLV=[(0x01:uuid),(0x04:user-agent)]]

Human-readable fallback (for logs): base64(cbor) or compact json: {v:1, f:5, c:"m:12a3", t:"9f4b..", r:2, m:["rid:..","ua:.."]}

API shape sketch for SDKs (JS/Python):
- CallGraphHeader.build({callerId, callStack, modelHint, policyBits, extra}) -> bytes
- CallGraphHeader.parse(bytes) -> {version, features, callerId, treeFp, hints, meta}

Call-tree semantics:
- A compact representation of the forward call chain: each node = short tool/function id + small ordinal. We collapse repeating paths using run-length or Bloom-ish fingerprinting to keep size down.
- Servers should be able to extract "leaf tool id" quickly for routing.

Routing hints (example enum):
- 0x00: none
- 0x01: prefer-low-latency
- 0x02: prefer-low-cost
- 0x03: require-region:EU (region encoded in TLV)
- 0x04: require-model-family (id in TLV)

Security and trust model:
- By default, header is advisory; untrusted clients can claim hints but servers enforce ACLs/policies server-side.
- Optional signed attachment (detached sig TLV) for enterprise/private deployments: a short sig over header + non-sensitive fields. Signature format should be small (ed25519 compact) and allow reference to attestation keys (KMS key id TLV).
- For on-prem customers, allow an HSM-backed signing policy that routers will trust for cost/priority overrides.

Compatibility / versioning:
- Version byte increments when wire layout changes incompatibly.
- Feature bitset: bits indicate supported optional encodings (e.g., bit0 = TLVv2, bit1 = signed-headers, bit2 = extended-caller). Clients set bits; servers read to decide whether to parse extras or ignore.
- TLV keys are namespaced with a registry and an escape mechanism for unknown keys (length prefixed) so older servers ignore unknown keys safely.

Telemetry / observability plan:
- Always emit the short tree fingerprint as part of request logs (low-cardinality).
- For sampling deeper call trees (for evals/debugging), include a debug trace endpoint that can request expanded call graph by request-id TLV.
- Expose metrics: fraction of requests carrying signed headers; distribution of header sizes; feature bit usage; top-10 caller ids.

Open questions / tradeoffs (brain dump):
- How to map arbitrary tooling stacks into a stable small id space? Maintain central registry vs hash-namespace? Registry gives semantics but requires sync. Hash allows offline but collisions/opacity.
- How aggressive to be in truncating the call-tree fingerprint? 64b risk of rare collisions but keeps size tiny.
- Should we compress repeated siblings or encode depth-first vs breadth-first? Simpler is depth-first linearized list with RLE for repeated nodes.
- Where to put request-id? If in TLV, we might duplicate it against network-level IDs. Advantage: header is self-contained for offline debugging.
- Backwards compatibility for older SDKs that don't set magic version: fall back to assumption v0 meaning no header.

Migration plan (rough):
1) Implement header builder/parsers in internal SDKs (js, py, go) behind feature flag.
2) Roll routers to accept unknown bitsets and ignore unknown TLV keys. Log unparsed keys for 2 weeks.
3) Release telemetry dashboard for header size & feature bits.
4) After 6 weeks of stable ops, flip default-on for new SDK versions and enable routing hints (soft-enforced).

Implementation notes / heuristics for parser:
- Prefer zero-copy parsing: parse fixed prefix in ~3 reads, then lazily parse TLV only if needed.
- Fail-safe: if header malformed, drop and record metric; do not block inference.
- Keep memory per-request bounded: cap TLV parse at N entries and size M bytes.

Mini-proto sketch (pseudo):
// LEB128-style varint for lengths
struct CallGraphHeaderV1 {
  u8 magic = 0x7A;
  u8 version = 1;
  varint features;
  bytes caller_id (len<=8) or 0;
  bytes tree_fp (len=8);
  u8 route_hint;
  TLV[] meta;
}

TLV key registry (examples):
- 0x01: request-id (uuid, 16 bytes or base64 short)
- 0x02: parent-call-id (8b)
- 0x03: region (short, e.g. "eu", "us")
- 0x04: user-agent (string <=64)
- 0x05: model-family (short id)
- 0x08: signature-ref (short key id)

Notes to self / TODOs:
- write JS/Go reference implementation + fuzz tests for truncation collisions
- propose short key registry process (owners, approvals) or use a hash-namespace with prefix map
- figure telemetry retention costs for storing tree fingerprints in logs vs separate trace store
- check alignment with existing trace/span ids (avoid duplication)
- sketch an admin UI for registries and feature bit rollout

References / inspiration:
- compact trace ids used by mobile SRE teams (internal)
- CBOR / LEB128 encodings for small-varint efficiency
- ed25519 compact signatures for minimal overhead

If this looks viable I'll flesh into a README + proto and a tiny reference lib. For now: experimental, optimistic, keep it small.
